examples.solution_text:
The variables are $y$, $x$ and $t$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=6x-2\\\frac{dy}{dt}&=\frac{dy}{dx}\times\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=(6x-2)\times2\end{align*}$
At $x=3$:
$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dt}&=(6(3)-2)\times2\\&=32\text{ units/s}\end{align*}$

The variables are $x$, $t$ and $u$. The intermediate variable is $t$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=8t-3\\\frac{dx}{du}&=\frac{dx}{dt}\times\frac{dt}{du}\\&=(8t-3)\times2\end{align*}$
At $t=4$:
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{du}&=(8(4)-3)\times2\\&=58\end{align*}$

Use the reciprocal derivative to reverse the rate link.
$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=3x^{2}+2\\\frac{dx}{dy}&=\frac{1}{3x^{2}+2}\\\frac{dx}{dt}&=\frac{dx}{dy}\times\frac{dy}{dt}\\&=\frac{-21}{3x^{2}+2}\end{align*}$
At $x=-2$:
$\begin{align*}\frac{dx}{dt}&=\frac{-21}{3(-2)^{2}+2}\\&=-\frac{3}{2}\text{ units/s}\end{align*}$
The negative rate means $x$ is decreasing.

examples.question_text: Given $y=5x^{2}-4x$ and $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=2$ units/s, find $\dfrac{dy}{dt}$ in terms of $x$.
Given $y=x^{3}$, where $x>0$, the rates at a certain instant are $\dfrac{dx}{dt}=4$ units/s and $\dfrac{dy}{dt}=108$ units/s. Find $x$ at that instant.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{align*}\frac{dy}{dx}&=3x^{2}\\\frac{dy}{dt}&=\frac{dy}{dx}\times\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=3x^{2}\times4\\&=12x^{2}\end{align*}$
Substitute the given rate of change of $y$:
$\begin{align*}108&=12x^{2}\\x^{2}&=9\end{align*}$
Since $x>0$, take the positive root:
$x=3$.

examples.question_text: A cube of ice remains cubic as it melts. Its edge length $s$ is decreasing at $3$ mm/min. Identify the three variables in a problem relating its volume to its edge length, and write the given rate with its sign.
examples.solution_text:
The variables are volume $V$, edge length $s$ and time $t$.
The edge length is decreasing, so its rate is negative:
$\dfrac{ds}{dt}=-3\text{ mm/min}$.

coverage.summary: Authored six examples covering five distinct assessed methods, including an additional forward-rate example with a renamed intermediate variable. Each has separate editable question and solution fields, single-dollar mathematics and aligned working. Solution prose and mathematics inherit the renderer's blue styling. No example requires a diagram or a bare-expression phantom gutter. All 28 assessment locators are mapped by method only; accepted assessment mathematics was neither changed nor re-audited. Source alignment and new-example calculations were checked against the supplied booklet. Independent review and actual rendering remain later stages; no files were written.

examples.derivation: Differentiating gives dy/dx = 6x − 2. The chain rule gives dy/dt = (6x − 2) × 2; at x = 3 this is 32 units/s. This follows the booklet example at lines 80–98.
dx/dt = 8t − 3, so dx/du = (8t − 3) × 2. At t = 4, dx/du = 58. The intermediate-variable chain matches Foundation Q2 at lines 131–134.

dy/dx = 3x² + 2, which equals 14 at x = −2 and is nonzero. Hence dx/dt = (dx/dy)(dy/dt) = −21/14 = −3/2 units/s. The reverse-rate task matches lines 121–129; the reciprocal method is explicitly taught at lines 337–358.
dy/dx = 10x − 4. Multiplying by dx/dt = 2 gives dy/dt = 20x − 8 units/s. Leaving the rate in terms of the variable follows lines 376–385, using the polynomial relationship taught at lines 80–98.
dy/dx = 3x², so dy/dt = 3x² × 4 = 12x². Substituting 108 gives x² = 9. The stated domain x > 0 selects x = 3. Solving an instantaneous variable from rates follows lines 714–718.
The three variables are volume V, edge length s and time t. A decrease of 3 mm/min means ds/dt = −3 mm/min. This adapts the interpretation activity at lines 201–208.

review.summary: All five distinct assessed methods are covered, and all 28 exact assessment locators are mapped appropriately. No syllabus exception is required. Accepted assessment mathematics was not re-audited. Final-size rendering remains for the later visual stage.
